citeAs: Singh, A., Natarajan, V., Shah, M., Jiang, Y., Chen, X., Batra, D., Parikh, D., & Rohrbach, M. (2019). Towards VQA Models That Can Read.
creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach (Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology)
description: TextVQA is a dataset containing 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reading and reasoning about text in the image to answer. It is designed to benchmark Visual Question Answering (VQA) models on their ability to read text in natural everyday scenes.
name: TextVQA
publisher: Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on most common answer for 97.9% questions.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three stage pipeline: 1) Annotators identify images that do not contain text. 2) Annotators provide 1-2 questions per image that require reading text to answer. 3) Annotators provide 10 answers for each question. Annotators were given options to flag images with no text, not a question, doesn't require reading, or unanswerable.
rai:dataBiases: Most questions start with 'what', frequently inquiring about 'time', 'names', 'brands' or 'authors'. The most common answer ('yes') is the majority answer for only 4.71% of the dataset, and 'yes/no' questions make up only 5.55% of the dataset.
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from the Open Images v3 dataset. Categories likely to contain text were identified by running the Rosetta OCR model on random samples to compute average OCR boxes, which were used as weights for sampling. A three-stage crowdsourcing pipeline was then used to filter images and collect questions and answers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from the Open Images v3 dataset, specifically from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard).
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images without text and noisy data from annotators were filtered out. Questions where a majority of workers marked flags (no text, not a question, doesn't require reading, unanswerable) were removed. Hand-crafted questions with known answers were used to identify and filter out bad annotators.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to aid visually impaired users by developing models capable of answering questions about everyday images that involve reading and reasoning about text in their surroundings.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking VQA models on their ability to read and reason about text in images, complementary to standard VQA datasets.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: The Rosetta OCR model was used to compute the average number of OCR boxes in image categories to determine sampling weights.
